Subject: Post-call recap + bench report (p50/p95/p99)

Alex — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and attached the micro-benchmark report we ran against a 4xA100-like configuration for the sample FastFin workload. Attachment: fastfin-bench-2026-07-27.pdf (PDF report).

Highlights from the bench (short):
- p50 token latency: ~12ms
- p95 token latency: ~46ms
- p99 token latency: ~120ms
- sustained throughput with batching: ~140 tokens/sec per replica at 2048-seq

Notes / assumptions:
- These numbers are single-model inference (no reranking) using our default batching policy; we used a 32-request batching window sampled to preserve latency SLOs.
- KV-cache warm start; cold-cache p99 is typically 1.6x higher in these runs.

Next steps I proposed on the call:
1) Neha to confirm the exact FastFin request mix and whether you want a throughput-optimized profile (higher batch, lower p99) vs strict latency profile.
2) If you want, we can run the same test inside your staging VPC (one-off) so you can see numbers on your infra.
3) Align on priority/timeline for a short pilot — 2 weeks to validate end-to-end.

If helpful, I can schedule a 20-minute slot for a live run demo (we can show live p99 charts + traces). Tell me what you want us to run (sample rate, seq length, keys).

Ben

Alex — quick follow-up with the technical clarifications we discussed on the call. I'm pasting the key config bits we used so you can reproduce or validate on your side.

Test setup summary:
- Model: open-variant-1.3 (FP16 quant run)
- Batch policy: adaptive (max batch size 64, batching window 30ms)
- Sequence length: 2048 tokens
- Hardware: 4 x A100 equivalent per replica with NVLink enabled
- Concurrency: 8 concurrent streams per replica for the sustained-throughput test

What drives the p99 in our runs: network jitter, cold KV cache, and occasional large requests that bypass batching. In our lab the p99 drops ~30-40% when you enable prefix caching for repeated contexts (your billing flows looked cache-friendly).

If you want to validate on your side, I can provide a run plan and a small artifact with our load generator settings. I attached a compressed capture of the server-side KV traces we sampled (fastfin-kvlogs-0729.tar.gz) — contains anonymized timing data and the run script.

If you prefer, we can also do a short hosted run where we spin up a sandbox model pinned to the same binaries and run your sample payloads. Typical turnaround: 48–72 hours once we have the sample traces.

Cheers,
